scope: Bounded evaluation of fixed-k Reciprocal Rank Fusion versus linear score combination under BEIR out-of-distribution shift

queries.query: reciprocal rank fusion out of distribution BEIR hybrid retrieval
Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet score calibration domain shift

evidence.claim: Out-of-distribution generalization when combining dense neural embeddings and lexical BM25 retrievers under domain shift was not evaluated
Zero-shot domain shift causes uncalibrated dense-retrieval similarity scales to diverge across corpora.
RRFscore(d in D) = sum_{r in R} 1 / (k + r(d)), with smoothing constant k = 60 fixed across experiments

closest_works.difference: Cormack et al. (2009) evaluated RRF only on in-distribution TREC collections without testing OOD neural-lexical score variance on BEIR.

candidates.claim: Rank-only Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) retains higher OOD NDCG@10 than uncalibrated min-max linear score fusion on BEIR
candidates.rationale: Cormack 2009 Section 3 explicitly leaves OOD dense-lexical hybrid fusion untested, and dual-regime closure search found no OOD boundary characterization.
candidates.consequence: Clarifies when rank fusion should replace score normalization in zero-shot hybrid retrieval
candidates.answer_path: Evaluate RRF vs linear fusion on frozen BEIR-OOD-Subset-v1 with verified NDCG@10 receipts
